fixes.explanation: Right, friend! The wives join in, and so do the sons and daughters who are able to understand (Nehemiah 10:28). The whole household is in on this oath. I love a full kitchen, and this is a full kitchen.

Close on the building theme, friend, but that's not this oath. What they swear here is "…to follow the Law of God given through His servant Moses…" (Nehemiah 10:29). Every city in Judah? That's a LOT of bricks for one afternoon.

Nope, friend, no gift basket for the king. A king of Persia isn't in this oath at all. They swear to follow the Law of God given through Moses and to obey all the commandments of the LORD (Nehemiah 10:29). This promise is made to their own God.

Good guess, friend, but "serve" isn't the word. The text says they will not give their daughters "…in marriage to the people of the land…" and will not take their daughters for their sons (Nehemiah 10:30). It's about marriage. Serving is a fine word, but it's in a different batch.

Clever, friend, but trading isn't in the text. They "…will not buy from them on a Sabbath or holy day." (Nehemiah 10:31). The promise is about not buying from the sellers on that day. The text doesn't say anything about swapping goods.
